events_chronological: As boys on the tenement streets, Nix and his friends Pilo, Squint and Nino run errands and petty rackets for the local boss Sallo.
Duke arrives in the neighbourhood, and after fighting each other the two boys join forces.
Nix watches Dinah dance alone through a peephole in the back of her father's delicatessen.
The boys begin rolling drunks and stash the proceeds in a case inside a station locker.
Sallo shoots Nino dead in the street, Nix knifes Sallo in return, and Nix is sent to prison.
Released years later, Nix finds Duke running a large bootlegging operation with Pilo and Squint.
The gang work for the union man Corrigan and the crooked police chief Vasari, whose newborn son they swap in the maternity ward.
Nix hires a deserted seafront restaurant for a night with Dinah, and rapes her in the car when she tells him she is leaving for the film capital.
The dry years end, and Duke, unwilling to stop, proposes robbing the federal bank.
Ruby and Nix agree that the only way to save Duke from himself is to have him arrested on a smaller job.
Nix telephones the police to tip them off, and is told at the scene that Duke, Pilo and Squint were shot dead and their bodies burned in the street.
Nix goes to the station locker for the gang's money, finds the suitcase empty, and leaves the city under another name.
In an opium den, Nix lies back and smiles at the ceiling.
Decades later Nix receives an invitation to the reinterment of his three friends in a mausoleum he never paid for.
Nix comes back to the city, finds Bunny still behind the delicatessen counter, and is given the key to the same locker.
Nix finds the mausoleum with his own name on the plaque and a suitcase of money inside, described as an advance on his next job.
Nix visits an aged Ruby at a retirement home endowed by Marrick, and she tells him Duke had wanted to die.
Nix finds Dinah backstage, now the cabinet minister Marrick's mistress, and she tries to send him away without letting him see her son.
Nix goes to Marrick's house and finds Duke alive, having stolen everything, now asking Nix to kill him.
Nix refuses to recognise him and walks away, and a garbage truck grinds past behind him as Duke disappears.
nonlinear_category_reason: Three eras of one man's life are entered and re-entered as blocks joined by an echoing sound or object, with no era dominant.
syuzhet_notes: The film cuts between three eras - boyhood, the bootlegging years and old age - without captions, carrying each jump on a sound or an object: a telephone that will not stop ringing, a thrown disc, a shot through a peephole. It opens in the middle era at told-order bullets 1-3, jumps decades forward at bullet 4, then all the way back at bullet 6, and thereafter alternates, so a childhood scene and an old man's return repeatedly sit side by side.
fabula_notes: The late-life frame may be an opium dream the protagonist is having in the middle era - the closing smile invites the reading and the film never settles it - and the ordering here takes the three eras as literally successive. The decades he spends hiding under another name are elided entirely, and his friend's survival is explained only in retrospect.
